topic: Perfect Forwarding and Universal References: Binding to Lvalues/Rvalues
explanation: Perfect forwarding efficiently passes arguments to functions or constructors without unnecessary copies or conversions.  It leverages universal references (T&&) which can bind to lvalues (objects with memory addresses) and rvalues (temporary objects). The compiler's implementation hinges on its ability to deduce the type of the argument and apply the appropriate forwarding mechanism, leveraging move semantics when possible.  This significantly impacts performance, especially with large or complex objects, reducing overhead compared to passing by value or reference.
